edits.text: Reading the lab pattern Biliary atresia — direct bilirubin high, GGT high, reticulocytes normal; well infant, pale stools, small or absent gallbladder · PFIC — direct bilirubin high with a paradoxically normal GGT; gallbladder present · HLH — direct bilirubin and GGT high but reticulocytes low from marrow failure; cytopenias, fever, an ill infant · Hemolysis — indirect bilirubin with high reticulocytes · Breast-milk jaundice — indirect, normal GGT and reticulocytes, normal stools and gallbladder · After Kasai — bile flow often fails over time; most children eventually need a liver transplant
edits.why: Distractor map for the source question: each option pattern tied to the disease it represents and why it fails here.

edits.anchor: Cholestasis is the right category of liver problem but the wrong bilirubin fraction.
edits.text: Unchecked attributePFIC also gives a direct hyperbilirubinemia, but its GGT is normal; a high GGT with an absent gallbladder is atresia.
edits.why: The most tempting distractor (25%) was PFIC; the GGT is the unchecked attribute.

edits.anchor: is the infant well, and is any of it direct?
edits.text: Hereditary Spherocytosis carries the Coombs-negative hemolysis pattern: indirect bilirubin with a high reticulocyte count.
